title: S0456 (2023 Regular): Possession or Use of a Firearm in a Sensitive Location

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Florida); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Florida text (Introduced, 2023-01-31; official copy, https://www.flsenate.gov/Session/Bill/2023/456/BillText/Filed/HTML (LegiScan doc 2671776))
provenance.note: Introduced version (filed 2023-01-31); later amendments are not in the text read. Quote shortens the list of sensitive locations (items (a)-(r) exist) and omits the exceptions in subsection (3) (law enforcement, security guards, military).

operative_text:
Section 1 (new s. 790.075, F.S.): (1) As used in this section, the term “sensitive location” means any of the following: (a) Any part of a health care facility licensed by the state, including a hospital, nursing home or other similar residential facility, or provider of services for the care, support, or treatment of individuals. (b) Any part of a building owned, leased, or operated by a governmental entity, including a polling place, courthouse, or law enforcement facility. (d) Any place of worship or religious observation. (n) Any educational institution, college or university, licensed private career school, school district, public school, private school, or charter school. (p) Any bar, restaurant where alcohol is served, or other site or facility where alcohol is sold for consumption on the premises.
Section 1 (new s. 790.075, F.S.): (2) Any other law notwithstanding, a person may not possess a firearm in a sensitive location. (a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), a person who violates this subsection commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084. (b) A person who discharges a firearm while violating this subsection commits a felony of the second degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.
